title: Caching, ISR & CDN Strategies
description: Understand the full Next.js cache system, on‑demand ISR, and edge caching for ultra‑fast delivery.

slides.title: The Next.js Cache Layer 🎂
slides.content:
# Multiple Levels of Caching

Next.js caches data at several levels:

1. **Router Cache** – client‑side, stores visited pages in memory.
2. **Full Route Cache** – server‑side, stores rendered HTML and RSC payload.
3. **Data Cache** – persists fetch results across requests and builds.
4. **Static Assets Cache** – images, fonts, JS bundles cached for a year.

Understanding these helps you design the perfect caching strategy.

slides.title: ISR & Time‑based Revalidation ⏰
slides.content:
# Stale‑While‑Revalidate

With ISR, you set a `revalidate` time on `getStaticProps`:

```js
return { props: { posts }, revalidate: 60 };
```

* The first request after 60 seconds triggers a background regeneration.
* Users see the stale (cached) page while the new one builds.
* Once built, the cache is swapped atomically.

This gives you static speed with dynamic freshness.

quizData.question: During ISR, what does the user see when a revalidation is triggered?

options.text: The previous (stale) version of the page

quizData.explanation: ISR serves the cached page first, then regenerates in the background. The next visitor gets the fresh page.

slides.title: On‑Demand ISR 🔄
Tag‑based Revalidation (app/actions.js)
slides.content: Use tags to revalidate multiple paths at once.

quizData.question: What is the advantage of `revalidateTag` over `revalidatePath`?

options.text: It can revalidate multiple paths associated with the same tag at once

quizData.explanation: Tags group caches across different routes. Revalidating a tag clears all related cached data, useful for collections like a product catalog.

slides.title: CDN & Edge Caching 🌍
slides.content:
# Serving from the Edge

When deployed to Vercel (or any platform with a CDN), your static pages and assets are distributed globally.

* **Static files** (JS, CSS, images) are cached for a year (immutable).
* **SSG pages** are cached at the edge until revalidated.
* **ISR pages** are cached at the edge and updated atomically.
* **`Cache-Control` headers** can be customised in `next.config.js`.

This means visitors from Tokyo, London, and New York all get content from a server near them – no extra work.

slides.title: Custom Cache-Control in next.config.js
slides.content: Set default headers for static assets or pages.

quizData.question: Why do CDN‑cached static assets improve Core Web Vitals?

options.text: They are served from a server geographically close to the user, reducing latency

quizData.explanation: A CDN stores copies of your files in multiple locations, so users download them from the nearest server, cutting download time and improving LCP.

slides.title: Cache Debugging 🔍
slides.content: Use the `Cache-Control` and `X-Nextjs-Cache` headers in the Network tab to understand cache hits and misses. Set `NEXT_PRIVATE_DEBUG_CACHE=1` as an env var for verbose logs.
